issues.legal_issue: A later statutory bar on challenging customary alienations does not defeat a possession claim that rests on a final declaratory decree obtained before the bar took effect.
material_facts: Reversioners obtained a declaratory decree that the gift was not binding on them, and that decree became final before the later possession suit.
The claimant sought possession on the basis that the final decree had left the gifted property free of the gift when the donor died; the claimant did not seek to challenge the gift anew.
The statutory amendment barring challenges to alienations contrary to custom was enacted after the declaratory decree.
issues.conclusion: The amendment did not bar the possession claim because the validity of the gift had already been finally determined and the claimant did not need to contest it again.
issues.legal_principle: Section 7 of the Punjab Customs (Power to Contest) Act, 1920, as amended by section 3 of the 1973 Amendment Act, bars a new challenge to an alienation on the ground that it is contrary to custom. It does not nullify a declaratory decree already obtained or prevent relief based on that decree. The Court approved Chand Singh v. Ind Kaur (1974) 1 P.L.R. 226 on the continued operation of an existing decree.

rule.if: possession_suit and prior_final_declaratory_decree and claim_relies_on_decree and no_new_customary_challenge

predicates.possession_suit: A claimant brings a suit seeking possession of property.
predicates.prior_final_declaratory_decree: A final declaratory decree concerning the alienation was obtained before the possession claim.
predicates.claim_relies_on_decree: The claimant bases the possession claim on the effect of the earlier decree.
predicates.no_new_customary_challenge: The claimant does not seek to contest the alienation anew on customary grounds.
predicates.amendment_bar_does_not_defeat_possession: The later bar on customary challenges does not prevent the possession claim from proceeding on the basis of the earlier final decree.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks possession based on an earlier final declaratory decree and does not raise a new customary challenge, the later bar on such challenges does not defeat the claim.

issues.legal_issue: A declaratory decree that an alienation is not binding enures to the benefit of persons entitled to share in the deceased alienor’s property as it stood at death, including a person who became an heir after the alienation.
material_facts: The donor’s gift was declared not binding on the reversioners, and the decree became final.
The claimant was adopted after the gift but before the donor died.
At the donor’s death, the property was free from the encumbrance of the gift, and the claimant was entitled to a share in the donor’s property as it then existed.
The claimant sought possession of the gifted property as an heir.
issues.conclusion: The earlier decree enured to the claimant’s benefit, and the claimant was entitled to possession of the gifted property.
issues.legal_principle: Section 8 of the Punjab Limitation (Custom) Act, 1920, provides that a decree declaring an alienation of ancestral immovable property not binding on the person who obtained it enures to the benefit of all persons entitled to impeach the alienation. Applying Giani Ram v. Ramji Lal (1969) 3 S.C.R. 944, the Court held that a declaratory decree restores the property to the alienor’s estate and benefits those entitled to a share in that estate as it existed at the alienor’s death; entitlement does not depend on whether the later heir could personally have challenged the alienation when it was made.

rule.if: inheritance_possession_claim and prior_final_declaratory_decree and property_free_from_alienation_at_death and claimant_entitled_to_share_at_death

predicates.inheritance_possession_claim: A person claiming through inheritance seeks possession of property formerly alienated by the deceased.
predicates.prior_final_declaratory_decree: A final decree declares the alienation not binding on the persons who obtained it.
predicates.property_free_from_alienation_at_death: The decree has left the property free from the alienation when the alienor dies.
predicates.claimant_entitled_to_share_at_death: The claimant is entitled to a share in the deceased’s property as it stood at death.
predicates.decree_benefits_claimant_entitled_at_dea: The decree enures to the benefit of a claimant entitled to share in the property at the deceased’s death.

issues.definition: When a final declaratory decree has freed property from an alienation by the time the alienor dies, it benefits an inheritance claimant entitled to share in the property at death.
